text:
elaine: heads up — i'm updating the terraform for the vectorizer svc to use IRSA + a KMS key for envelope-encryption. helm chart deploys the k8s serviceaccount via postrender, so i'm worried the key grant might race if we try to create it in the same plan. any quick checks?

sam: do you have the TF snippet you plan to apply? postrender usually creates the SA during release, so ordering from TF side can be tricky.

elaine: paste below — it's simple:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "vector_sa" {
  name = "vector-svcaccount"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "vector_key" {
  description = "vector data key"
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "vector_sa_grant" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.vector_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vector_sa.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt"]
}
```

miguel: small concern — if the helm postrender creates a k8s serviceaccount, TF's aws_iam_role (IRSA) is separate but you might be relying on the SA annotation (eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn) timing. The grant uses the IAM role ARN directly, so TF ordering is OK, but the AWS principal that assumes the role needs to exist before the pod uses it. Are you attaching the annotation via helm?

elaine: yes helm sets the annotation on the SA. the race i'm worried about is when we create the grant referencing the IAM role ARN but the SA annotation/role binding isn't applied yet in-cluster, then pods start and fail decrypt. also ops asked that grants use a Condition to lock to the cluster arn.

anna: for the condition, you'll want something like: 
```json
"Condition": {
  "StringLike": {
    "aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:iam::*:role/eks-role/*"
  }
}
```
but for IRSA it's usually better to tie to the OIDC provider + sub claim via the key policy if you need stronger scoping.

sam: another approach: keep the aws_kms_grant in TF but add a null_resource with a local-exec that waits for the SA annotation to appear in the cluster before applying the grant. e.g. `kubectl get sa vector -n infra -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn}'` and loop until present. then make the grant depend_on the null_resource. cheap and effective.

miguel: agreed. or flip it: create the SA+annotation in TF (if you can manage the SA manifest as part of k8s provider) so TF sees the ordering natively. but helm postrender is convenient for chart ownership.

elaine: good notes — i'll try the null_resource wait for now. quick sanity check on the grant semantics: does `grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vector_sa.arn` work even if role is IRSA (i.e., OIDC federation)?

sam: yes — the role exists in IAM either way. IRSA means the role's assume policy trusts OIDC, but the role ARN is the principal for KMS grants. KMS doesn't care about federation.

anna: also make sure the key policy allows the account root + the grant, otherwise Decrypt may still fail. we had a gotcha where grants didn't override a restrictive key policy.

deploy-bot: deploy-notice: staging vector release v1.12 started (helm) — will create SA `vector` in `infra`.

elaine: perfect timing — i'll delay applying the grant until the postrender finishes and null_resource confirms the annotation. i'll open a PR and tag @sam for review, include the wait helper and a note about key policy checks.

sam: thanks! if you want i can pair on the wait script, i have one we used for payments.

elaine: pls — that'd speed things. i'll DM to coordinate. :thumbsup:

miguel: also leave a comment in the PR about why we chose grant+wait vs key policy-only. helps future readers.

elaine: will do.
